reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: I don’t know if it’s just me because it seems like this has great reviews, but I need the signs to be slower so I can actually see them. I need somebody to show me how to actually move my hands and fingers because just watching somebody when the signs start very close to the chest or body it’s impossible to see their hand movement. I don’t know. I guess I’m just a terrible learner or an idiot but this isn’t the way I can learn.

reviews.title: Why limit the lessons!?
reviews.text: Why is Lingvano limiting how many BSL lessons I do a day? If you want to learn quickly this is not the app you want, it’s great for a slow build up but with just one lesson a day it’s hardly pushing yourself.

reviews.title: Terrible app
reviews.text: Super unclear. Each person modeling their n the app signs very differently. They ask you to answer questions on signs before they teach it to you. The alphabet used is very different from the alphabet most of us learned in school. Very difficult to see hand positions in videos and they move extremely fast even on the slow mode. Deleted the app and tried to give it another chance. Total waste of money

reviews.title: ASL learning
reviews.text: The best app there is to learn ASL, I’m only two days in and can hold an average conversation. I definitely recommend this to any consistent learners.

reviews.title: Would be great. Isn’t
reviews.text:
Mostly fantastic for learners, though it’s a shame that there are a few errors on some lessons. However, why encourage daily use (to keep your streak) if there is limited content. In 60 days, with 3-10 min use daily, there is no content left and no details about any new material being made. Shame
I’ve now got a paid for app and nothing to learn.

reviews.title: Not accessible to low income
reviews.text: It would be great if there was an unpaid version available. I would like to learn it I am unemployed making this a “luxury item” for me.

reviews.title: Payment for Lessons
reviews.text: I understand the need for money to keep your business going, but sometimes it goes too far. I don’t mind spending some money for lessons, but 20 dollars a month? 50 dollars every three months or 120 dollar annually, to learn sign language? You can only get through the few lessons of the second chapter on unit one before it locks you out of progressing before paying their ridiculous prices. Most people that want to learn sign language via an app, or mostly doing it for fun, or for inclusivity. To lock that behind such a huge paywall is insane.

I enquired about the lack of content and was ignored twice. Even their dictionary is limited compared to other apps. Such a shame!

reviews.title: GREAT BUT
reviews.text: I have a deaf and hard of hearing program at my school and they like to talk with me but I did not know sign language I got this app and started getting the hang of sign language I love this app now I can easily understand the sign language but the thing is I am in middle school I cannot do the subscription and now I only have one chapter and then part of one because I have to pay  to keep using it and that is insane. I made a friend who is hard of hearing and it’s very hard for us to talk so the one thing I want to be changed is please make the app free and just use ads instead because I think a language that is many people’s main way to communicate should be free for others to learn

reviews.title: In app purchases required
reviews.text:
So far the app itself had been pretty great! Easy format, easy to understand, useful language. But after about 2 hours of lessons it does not allow you to progress unless you subscribe. Not even duolingo is that predatory, at least you can go on each day and try. With Lingvano you reach a certain lesson or process point access is revoked; which is ironic because hearing people being able to easily access ASL lessons directly creates more accessibility for the deaf community, but I digress. 
It would be an absolutely wonderful tool for the hearing to learn ASL, if it wasn’t behind a predatory paywall. Thank you for doing nothing for the deaf community.

reviews.title: Not enough content
reviews.text: I really want to learn sign language so I signed up for a year and then realised that the content is very limited. Three months content at best. I feel like I’ve been conned. I could have just subscribed for three months and completed all the content and cancelled my subscription.

reviews.title: Subscription Scam
reviews.text: Making everything in life a subscription is a scam. This is sign language, not a regular language. Some people are born deaf, some become deaf from things they can’t control and forcing people to pay to learn when it’s out of their control is unethical and literally tone deaf. It only allowing you to go up to chapter 2, then everything else is locked and you can only review what you already did is trash. This app is garbage and the creators are greedy monsters. Don’t use apps. Please use ASL lifeprint with Bill Vicars. It’s completely free and what I was using originally but wanted something easier to carry around a practice on the go but. Every. Single. App. Is a subscription. Remember when the iPhones came out and you could just pay however much for an app and then you get everything with it, and if the app was free then so were the contents within the app. Greed has taken over this world. I want to create a fully free sign language app so if anyone is interested….

reviews.title: Another paywall app
reviews.text: I downloaded this from an Instagram ad with an interest in learning BSL. I was immediately met upon opening with a subscription, which I didn’t mind. I declined it and started to learn and found it extremely helpful, until the app told me that I wasn’t able to continue if I didn’t subscribe. The subscription should be OPTIONAL, not dependant on the app as a whole, especially when it’s advertised as free. I will be deleting the app and finding alternative places to learn BSL. I’m so disappointed

reviews.title: Shop around
reviews.text: After an 800 day streak I reached out on multiple occasions to see what the designers and tech support could figure out should be next steps for learning as well as errors within their system.   There’s a strong disconnect between my account and experiences and customer service which is why I have to rate them low.  The app is fun for a bit and I’m thrilled asl is making headway as a language but I think there are much better ways to teach asl via an app like this.  Pros for the app would be a basic dictionary - good video list - and going through the entire curriculum once.  Extreme cons would be it’s not worth $120 after you finish, it’s a dead end or you’re told to pay for live sessions, no connection to other users, no fun review sessions (just out of context vocab) it’s clear they’re still figuring out bugs in app coding and how to better integrate lessons through live sessions or AI and video readers (like timed finger spelling) and the customer service being meh.  If they can figure out those items it’ll be a great app until then shop around.  So as someone that has invested hundreds of hours in this app I’m quitting, trying to remember the best part before this bad breakup. There’s a lot more ASL app competition now worth a comparison review before you buy than there was when I started 800 days ago and at this point I’m happy to move on advising others shop around first.
